Notes: Lower half of the cushion centerpiece: a softened square that swells at the waist and rolls under toward the wrist, like the belly of a cushion-cut gem, with a beaded line around the parting line. 1.0 mm walls.
Upper half: two crisp polished Art Deco tiers step up to an oval halo of 26 small white stones with a beaded edge, around a polished bezel that holds the opalite.
Oval opalite (glass moonstone) cabochon, bezel-set like a gemstone. Milky white in daylight; it glows warm amber from the LEDs underneath when your group is near, and red for SOS.

Bluetooth 5.0 microcontroller with onboard LiPo charger (BQ25101) and 5 µA sleep. Runs the buttons, Bluetooth finding, LEDs and motor. Stacked on the LoRa module on 1.5 mm low-profile headers. ~$9.90 direct from Seeed.
Semtech SX1262, 862–930 MHz, 22 dBm, 1.6 µA sleep. Mounts under the XIAO on 1.5 mm low-profile headers. U.FL antenna connector. ~$9.90 direct from Seeed.

Small FPC antenna with U.FL pigtail, curved along the inside back wall of the centerpiece, away from the wrist. The resin shell lets the signal out; in a production gold piece the band itself becomes the antenna.
Four addressable mini LEDs on a 13 mm flex strip right under the stone, one data pin (D7). In finding mode the stone brightens and the number lit (1–4) shows how close you are; red means SOS.

Low-profile 3 × 3 × 1.5 mm tactile switch (260 gf, so it does not fire in a bag) under a polished gold firefly wing that folds down over the left shoulder of the centerpiece, with a fine engraved vein. Plain wing = Find.
Same switch under the right wing, which carries a small prong-set white stone so it feels different under your finger in the dark. Hold 3 s for SOS.

3.7 V, 4 × 12 × 30 mm with protection circuit, hidden in the clasp box under the wrist and wired to the centerpiece through the hollow band. About 26 h at the modeled 4.1 mA average. Charges in about 1.5 h.
3 V ERM coin motor (0820) in the clasp box, pressed against the skin side, so the hot/cold pulse is felt right on the underside of the wrist. Switched by a small MOSFET.
Flush 2-pin magnetic receptacle on the outside of the clasp box, with a USB cable that snaps on. No port to seal, so the bangle stays splash-proof.

Rounded capsule at the bottom of the bangle that hides the battery and motor and doubles as the push clasp. A beaded line at the waist matches the centerpiece; small polished rondelles finish the wire ends.

Part: Driver parts: MOSFET, diode, resistors, JST-PH
Notes: AO3400 (or 2N7002) N-channel MOSFET, 1N4148 flyback diode, resistors 10 kΩ ×2, 3.3 kΩ, 15 kΩ, 330 Ω, 100 Ω, 47 µF capacitor, JST-PH 2-pin. One assortment kit covers ten bands.

Two slim hollow 18k gold-plated wires (Ø2.2 mm, 1.8 mm apart) that sweep around the wrist, joined by a small hinge barrel at the side, with polished rondelles where they meet the centerpiece and the clasp. The battery leads run inside one wire.
34 AWG enamelled wire for the battery run through the band, 30 AWG silicone wire, Kapton tape, 1 mm foam to stop rattle, silicone gasket cord.
